expected_fault: R2's NTP master stratum was changed from 3 to 15 (the worst valid stratum value in Cisco IOS, one below the protocol's reserved "unsynchronized" value of 16). Since NTP clients normally synchronize at one stratum above their time source, R3 recalculated its own stratum to match (15) after its next poll. Packet Tracer's NTP simulation did not reject or flag the degraded stratum as invalid -- R3 continued reporting "synchronized" with R2 as its selected system peer, meaning a severely degraded time source can silently propagate through an NTP hierarchy without triggering any visible error on client routers.
ai_root_cause: Administrator changed the NTP master configuration on R2 from a valid stratum (3) to an invalid high stratum (15), causing R2 to advertise stratum 15 and its clients (R3) to adopt stratum 15 as well
ai_evidence: R2# show ntp status before fault shows "stratum 3"; after applying "no ntp master 3" and "ntp master 15", R2# show ntp status reports "stratum 15". R3# show ntp status after fault shows "stratum 15" and its association line shows "15" as the remote stratum ("*~192.168.77.209   127.127.1.1   15 ..."). This directly ties the configuration change on R2 to the degraded stratum on R3.
ai_fix_steps: Enter configuration mode on R2 | Remove the incorrect master command: no ntp master 15 | Re‑apply the correct master stratum: ntp master 3 | Exit configuration mode | Verify with show ntp status on R2 and R3
